subject: Tenor blend crossover: proposed top-up & co-term approach
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: ops@acme.ai; contracts@acme.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Tenor blend crossover: proposed top-up & co-term approach

Hi Ana / Team,

Following our call this morning, attaching a concise proposal that aims to: 1) transition Acme from a straight annual prepay to a blended annual+usage model over 18 months, 2) co-term the larger Robotics account with the Platform contract on 2028-01-01, and 3) provide a triggered top-up buffer for Q1 bursts tied to run-rate milestones.

High-level summary in the sheet: two ramp profiles (conservative / accelerated), a soft auto-renew opt-out at 90 days, and a burst credit pool that unlocks when average monthly tokens exceed 120% of baseline for two months. Pricing preserves current committed unit rates for the committed portion and applies a blended rate to variable usage.

Action items I recommend for this week:
- Ops: confirm whether the burst buffer should be measured on rolling 30-day or calendar-month basis (we recommended rolling 30-day).
- Procurement: confirm whether you need legal redlines in the SOW or a separate amendment (we can do either).
- Internal: Marissa / Karthik please review the attached schedule and draft SOW.

Attachments: Proposed_Term_Schedule_ACME_v3.xlsx, SOW_Amendment_ACME_draft.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147
From: Ana Cortez <ops@acme.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, contracts@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenor blend crossover: proposed top-up & co-term approach

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the files. A few clarifying questions from ops before we loop legal: 

1) For the burst buffer trigger, can you confirm the lookback window where you expect us to report? We’re leaning calendar-month to align with our billing, but open to rolling 30-day if it reduces false positives.

2) For the co-term, we have an internal fiscal cadence that prefers 2028-04-01 rather than Jan 1. Would shifting to April materially change any of the pricing tiers?

3) How would overage reconciliation work under the blended model — immediate invoice vs monthly true-up?

We’ll review the SOW draft and send procurement comments next.

Best,
Ana Cortez
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Robotics
ops@acme.ai
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ana Cortez <ops@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, contracts@acme.ai
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Tenor blend crossover: proposed top-up & co-term approach

Ana — great questions, answers inline below.

1) Burst buffer lookback: we recommend rolling 30-day because it smooths end-of-month spikes and works better with the runtime's auto-burst policy. That said, if your billing system requires calendar-month measurement, we can align and adjust the unlock threshold by +5% to compensate for greater variance.

2) Co-term date: moving to 2028-04-01 is fine. The pricing tiers are stable; the only practical change is the ramp schedule alignment — we’ll shift milestone checkpoints by three months (see Attached v3 sheet, tab 'Milestones - April'). No rate delta.

3) Overage reconciliation: monthly true-up is the simplest operational model and what most customers prefer. We propose a monthly true-up invoice (30-day net) with a capped per-period smoothing credit on first reconciliation to avoid sticker shock.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Publish v3 with an alternate 'Milestones - April' tab and one-page summary for Procurement.
- Prep a short amendment template that references the existing contract and captures the blended-rate calculation and unlock mechanics (we included a first-draft in the SOW_Amendment_ACME_draft.pdf).

For legal/procurement: we can either produce a redline-ready amendment or, if you prefer, issue a new SOW tied to the master agreement. Which do you prefer?

Thanks — I’ll target an updated file by Friday EOD PST.

Thanks everyone — Ana, appreciate the timing note re: April. Karthik / I reviewed the April-aligned schedule and the SOW draft. Quick internal decisions and asks so we can land this next week: 

- Confirmed: co-term = 2028-04-01 (no pricing change).
- Confirmed: burst buffer measured on calendar-month (per Acme preference) with the +5% threshold adjustment Jonas noted.
- Procurement preference: amendment rather than new SOW (simpler for existing MA). Please accept the amendment template and mark any clauses you need redlined.

Karthik — can you run a final ARR impact snapshot using the 'accelerated' ramp profile and include a short one-pager we can attach to the amendment (legal likes to see ARR movement)? Target EOD Wed.

Ana / Contracts — once you send back procurement comments we’ll cut an internal approval path (rev ops + finance) and send a DocuSign link for the amendment. I’ve added the one-pager and the updated schedule to the shared hub link below.

Related: HubSpot deal ACME-2026-1073, SOW and amendment drafts in attachments. DocuSign link will be shared after procurement comments.

Thanks,
